//: SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT OR Apache-2.0 — Postern Comms (Enterprise) data-residency options. NOT LEGAL ADVICE. Residency choice has legal consequences (adequacy, transfer mechanisms) that require legal review — this file only declares the DEPLOYMENT options honestly.

options.label: European Union
options.crossBorderTransfer: None by default. Any transfer outside the EEA requires an Art. 44-49 mechanism (adequacy decision / SCCs) — legal review required.
options.notes: Recommended default for EU-employed data subjects.

options.label: Brazil
options.crossBorderTransfer: International transfer governed by LGPD Arts. 33-36 (adequacy, SCCs, specific consent) — legal review required.
options.notes: Recommended for BR-employed data subjects. ANPD is the supervisory authority.

options.label: Self-hosted / on-premises (customer-controlled)
options.regulation: Determined by the customer's own jurisdiction & deployment
options.crossBorderTransfer: Entirely under the customer's control; the customer is the controller and sets residency.
options.notes: Postern Labs operates no server in this mode. The customer holds all stores. This is the strongest residency guarantee and the E2EE story is unchanged.

rails: Residency is a DEPLOYMENT config, not a legal opinion. Choosing 'eu' does not by itself make a deployment GDPR-compliant.
E2EE means message CONTENT is unreadable by the operator in every residency mode; residency affects where CIPHERTEXT and METADATA physically live.
Cross-border transfer of personal data is a legally gated act — the transfer mechanism must be reviewed by counsel before enabling.
